note: The Levee District ran from Eighteenth Street to Twenty-second, Wabash to Clark, 'several blocks away from Prairie Avenue'; the Everleigh Club and 'Vic Shaw's resort' were the preeminent brothels, Shaw's 'existing on Prairie Avenue for a time'; the sisters were born Simms, inherited some $35,000, ran a house in Omaha, and took the name Everleigh from their grandmother's 'Everly yours'; the club at 2131-2133 South Dearborn occupied two mansions with 50 rooms (the Japanese Throne Room, the Mirror Room, the Silver Parlor); champagne cost $12 'in an era when an entire meal could be had for fifty cents'; the entrance fee was $50; the women were called 'butterflies'. It names Marshall Field, Jr. among famed clients and says rumours persisted for years that he was shot there; it is a blog, and the clients it names are its say.
what_it_supplies: the Everleigh Club's address, rooms and prices
what_it_does_not_supply: any named Prairie Avenue client in 1904, as fact
